title: Story to screen
summary: Follow topo story preview from committed story intent to generated browser files. These arrows are an authored trace of actual calls, data handoffs, and error propagation—not package dependencies or compiler-derived control flow. The selected catalogue is rendered as a set; individual stories resolve/render in parallel. Preview launches neither a model nor a browser/server.

sections.title: Request preview
sections.body:
Owner: @topo/cli, runCli.

Input: topo story preview <repository> <story>. Check argument count and the initialized cache/site/index.html before doing work. The requested path is checked for membership AFTER buildCatalogue returns; it does not restrict rendering to one story.

Stories must be committed and unchanged. Repository source may be dirty; successful preview warns that evidence describes the working tree. No scanner or model is invoked by this branch.

sections.title: Load stories + snapshot
sections.body:
Owner: @topo/cli.

Capture Git revision, status/diff fingerprint and history depth. Read committed stories, apply catalogue.storyIds when configured, and reject changed selected story documents. Capture each distinct referenced source file once.

The stable reader rejects escaped paths, symlinks, non-files, replaced files, or files changing during a read. A missing file is recorded as absent and rejected during anchor resolution. This is a bounded source snapshot, not a compiler build.

sections.title: Resolve evidence
sections.body:
Owner: @topo/story.

For each selected story, resolve every source anchor from the captured bytes. When a SHA-256 is authored, compare the whole file. Resolve requested symbols and exact excerpts; derive current line ranges and evidence text.

Missing files/symbols/patterns, ambiguous patterns, and stale hashes fail explicitly. Successful resolution proves structure and evidence existence, not the narrative's truth or completeness.

sections.title: Render each story
sections.body:
Owner: @topo/diagram-core.

The catalogue's default renderer delegates to renderStory. An explicit graphviz story selects Graphviz; otherwise the adapter verifies the pinned Archify runtime, builds its typed specification, calls native deliver, and applies Topocode's viewer adaptations.

Return HTML, renderer provenance, and backend-owned assets in memory. The catalogue adds source evidence and renderer receipts. Promise.all runs resolution/rendering per selected story; one rejected story prevents publication of the set.

sections.title: Still current and selected?
sections.body:
Owner: @topo/cli.

After rendering, reread anchor files and compare Git revision, dirty state, and the status/diff fingerprint. runCli then checks that the requested story is in the built catalogue. writeBuiltCatalogue checks freshness again before acquiring the workspace lock.

Changed evidence or a missing selected story refuses publication. These are explicit pre-publication checks, not a continuously held source-code lock.

sections.title: Stage + replace output
sections.body:
Owners: @topo/cli composes output; @topo/workspace controls publication.

Acquire the workspace write lock. Inside withGeneratedTransaction, generate Home, story wrappers, viewer HTML, navigation/theme scripts, evidence and renderer assets; queue obsolete generated files for retirement.

writeGenerated collects bytes in the transaction. Prepare staged files/backups and check destination contents before replacing files. Authored stories and repository source are not rewritten. Lock acquisition and preparation failures stop before replacing the generation.

sections.title: Ready to browse
sections.body:
Output: .topo/cache/site/ contains the refreshed selected catalogue, rendered viewers, source evidence, and provenance.

The CLI prints the selected story's generated path and a topo serve instruction. It does NOT launch a server or browser. An already-running local server can show the new generation after refresh; static hosting is a separate topo bundle/deployment step.

Generated cache is disposable. Committed stories, configuration, and repository source remain the durable inputs.

sections.title: Stop before publication
sections.body:
An input, snapshot, anchor, renderer, freshness, selection, lock, or preparation error propagates as failure. Do not label it as a successful preview or replace existing viewer content with plausible fallback output.

These branches occur before replacing the generation. Fix the reported cause, then run preview again. Temporary locks/staging are not a promise that no transient filesystem activity occurred.

sections.title: Attempt rollback
sections.body:
Owner: @topo/workspace.

On a reported replacement error, walk already-committed replacements in reverse and restore backups (or remove newly created files). The original error is rethrown.

Rollback can itself fail: report an AggregateError and preserve rollback files for repair. This is rollback-capable publication, not crash-atomicity and not an unconditional guarantee that the prior generation survived.

connections.label: initialized
connections.rationale: The preview branch checks the site and awaits buildCatalogue(root).

connections.label: bad request / no site
connections.rationale: Argument and site-index preconditions throw before catalogue generation.

connections.label: captured bytes
connections.rationale: The captured snapshot loader is passed to resolveStoryDocument for each selected document.

connections.label: resolved story
connections.rationale: Each resolved document is awaited before renderer.render(resolved) is called.

connections.label: missing / stale anchor
connections.rationale: Anchor failures reject that story's Promise and prevent the catalogue from reaching publication.

connections.label: all artifacts ready
connections.rationale: After every render succeeds and duplicate IDs are checked, buildCatalogue calls assertCatalogueCurrent.

connections.label: renderer failure
connections.rationale: Backend errors and unsupported artifact types reject catalogue construction; no fallback viewer is published.

connections.label: yes
connections.rationale: A current catalogue containing the requested story is passed through the second freshness check into the workspace lock and publication.

connections.label: no
connections.rationale: Changed anchor bytes/Git state or missing requested membership throws instead of publishing stale output.

connections.label: replacement succeeds
connections.rationale: After successful generated publication, runCli prints the rendered story and serve instruction.

connections.label: lock / preparation error
connections.rationale: A busy lock or failed preparation does not reach the replacement loop.

connections.label: replacement error
connections.rationale: Reported failures in the replacement loop restore already-committed files in reverse; incomplete rollback is explicitly reported.
